data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Vitamins & trace elements_

**Class:** Fat-soluble antioxidant vitamin (α-tocopherol)

## Mechanism of action
- Lipid-phase antioxidant — protects cell membranes from lipid peroxidation; regenerated by vitamin C

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Adjunct in cutaneous lupus, yellow nail syndrome, epidermolysis bullosa, claudication (weak evidence)
- Reduces dapsone-induced haemolysis/methaemoglobinaemia (adjunct)
- Topical: moisturiser and antioxidant in cosmetics, scars (no proven benefit), photoprotection booster

## Dose & formulations
- Oral 400–800 IU/day; topical in creams/oils

## Adverse effects
- High oral doses: bleeding tendency (antiplatelet), possible increased mortality with very high doses
- Topical: allergic contact dermatitis, contact urticaria, erythema multiforme-like reactions

## Contraindications
- Bleeding disorders, anticoagulant therapy (high doses)

## Drug interactions
- Warfarin (increased bleeding)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe at dietary doses.

## Viva points
- Topical vitamin E is a recognised contact allergen; no proof it improves scars

_Sources: Khopkar (Vitamin E — tocopherol; topical vitamins); Wolverton 4e ch.57. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
